core.title: Give every wagon produce[] and consume[] entry its required fields
core.given: A wagon definition with produce[] and/or consume[] artifact lists
core.when: The planner adds or edits a produce[] or consume[] entry
core.then: Every produce[] entry declares name, contract and telemetry (optional: to, urn, version), and every consume[] entry declares name (optional: from, contract, telemetry, urn, version).
prefer: Write the contract and telemetry keys on every produce[] entry, even when their values are null, as for an internal artifact (to: internal)
Give produce[].to only internal or external; omitting it means external
avoid: Leaving out contract or telemetry keys on a produce[] entry
A consume[] entry with no name
Fields other than the listed required/optional ones on produce[] or consume[] entries
A from value outside wagon:<slug>|system:<service>|appendix:<type>|internal, or a to value other than internal|external
core.why: Produce/consume entries are the declared artifact interface that contract, data-flow, semantic and telemetry-ownership checks resolve against, so their shape must be uniform.
evidence: Each produce[] entry has the name, contract and telemetry keys present, and only the optional keys to/urn/version beyond them; null contract/telemetry values, as for an internal artifact (to: internal), are allowed
Each consume[] entry has the name key present and only the optional keys from/contract/telemetry/urn/version beyond it
to values are internal or external; from values, when present, match wagon:slug|system:service|appendix:type|internal
verification: A static check scans each wagon-definition manifest (discovered by path and file kind, per the plan-artifact role in the profile) and validates every produce[] and consume[] entry against the required/optional field lists in then: produce[] requires name, contract, telemetry, with optional to (internal|external, default external), urn, version; consume[] requires name, with optional from (wagon:slug|system:service|appendix:type|internal), contract, telemetry, urn, version

Required means the key is declared on the entry; the check imposes no non-null constraint and must not reject an entry whose contract/telemetry keys are present with null values (an allowed case, not an exhaustive nullability rule)
A missing produce[].to is treated as external

Entry-level activation (a produce[] or consume[] entry added or modified) needs a diff-level observer of the manifest format; when no such observer is available, that is an observation limitation of the check — entry-level changes go unobserved and the rule does not thereby fire. Activation is not broadened: the check does not fall back to validating wagon-definition edits outside produce[]/consume[] (for example description-only edits), which remain out of scope

values: produce[] or consume[] entry added or modified

fires: Planner adds a new produce[] entry to a wagon definition
Planner adds or edits a consume[] entry that declares an upstream artifact
Planner authors a new wagon with both produce and consume lists
doesNotFire: Editing wagon fields outside produce[]/consume[] (e.g. description only)
Editing contract or telemetry schema files themselves without touching wagon produce/consume entries
Code or test changes that do not touch wagon definitions

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kind (and format) of the wagon-definition manifest that the rule's file_kind activation fact and the check's discovery scope to; the core itself names no file kind, format, suffix or path.

neutralityNotes: The manifest schema itself — the produce[]/consume[] field lists and the from/to value grammar (wagon:<slug>|system:<service>|appendix:<type>|internal; internal|external) — is the ATDD planning-manifest schema this rule imposes, not a stack mechanic, so it is kept verbatim in the core; it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, file suffix or path. 'wagon' is retained as the ATDD planning concept of a bounded slice (the vocabulary itself models it via layout.wagon_dir and the urn.wagon parameter); the concrete manifest file kind and format ('wagon manifest / wagon definition YAML', found by path and file kind) are stack facts delivered through the profile (roles.plan_artifact.kinds), and the needs_new_observer note's 'diff-level YAML observer' is neutralized to a diff-level observer of the manifest format, whose absence is reported as an observation limitation without broadening activation. The source's concrete example entries (commons:ux:foundations, internal:cache, wagon:maintain-ux) and the term ids produce_fields/consume_fields have no stack-neutral equivalent and stay in the Bun realization.
